the presence of the elongation factor EF-Tu and EF- G does not contribute drastically, if at all, to substrate selectivity at high [Mgt+], polyleucine synthesis being accelerated by both factors to roughly the same degree.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanism of the ribosomal poly(U)direct-ed polyleucine synthesis.
the study of ribosomal misreading of the genetic code.
the study of the mechanism of ribosomal synthesis of polypeptide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
poly(U)directedly ribosomes synthesize polypeptide chains in which leucyl residues predominate.

ribosomal synthesis of polyphenyalanine on poly(U) as a template is much more efficient than polyleucin synthesis, that EF-TU and EF-G are involved in the synthesis of polyphenyialanine but not in polyleucine synthesis and that the presence of EF-TU and/or EF-G does not affect the selectivity of polypeptide synthesis on poly(U) at high [Mgl+].
the elongation factors are not essential for poly(U)-directing polyleucine synthesis, but they accelerate this process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
poly(U) is a good template for synthesis of polypheylalanine but a bad template for synthesis of polyleucine.

polyleucine synthesis in the presence of EF-Tu and EF-6 is about 10-fold slower than polyphenylalanin synthesis, while in the absence of elongation factors polyleucine is synthesized 30-times slower than polyphenyIalanine.
the selectivity of translation is determined primarily by the tRNA and the codon-anticodon interaction, and the elongation factors are involved only in the regulation of the rate of translation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ribosomes can be programmed to synthesize polypeptides with a single amino acid, and the efficiency of the process depends on the identity of the amino acid in the codon and the identity of the tRNA carrying the amino acid.
the ribosomal machinery is not completely specific with respect to the amino acid sequence of the growing polypeptide chain.
polyleucine synthesis can be performed in the absence of both elongation factors.
